description: Pinned immutable authorities for WASM-GEMM-GNAF. SPEC.md section 4.

wasmCore.note: Vendored from the official WebAssembly/spec repository at the pinned commit. SPEC 5 requires offline verification to recompute pins from CONTENT rather than trust a checksum string. TWO manifests do that, and the second is the stronger one. SHA256SUMS records every vendored file's SHA-256; recomputing it proves the tree has not changed since this repository wrote it down. BLOBS records every vendored file's GIT BLOB OBJECT ID -- sha1("blob " + len + NUL + content), a function of the bytes alone -- which is the identity the pinned commit's own tree lists each file under, so recomputing it proves the bytes are the ones commit 9d36019973201a19f9c9ebb0f10828b2fe2374aa names. Both are rechecked offline by `just vendor`, with no network and no git invocation.
wasmCore.scope: THREE parts. (1) specification/wasm-3.0/ -- the 35 normative SpecTec sources, which is where the grammar and typing rule BODIES live: 5.3-binary.instructions.spectec carries the actual opcode bytes, 2.3-validation.instructions.spectec the typing rules including stack polymorphism. (2) document/core/{binary,valid,exec,syntax,appendix} -- the 39 rendered normative sources the conformance map cites by label; these only REFERENCE the rule bodies, as unexpanded $${grammar:} / $${rule:} macros. (3) test/core/ -- the 299 official conformance test files, including the simd, gc, exceptions, bulk-memory, multi-memory, memory64 and relaxed-simd suites. Vendoring (2) alone, which is what this pin held before, left every rule body outside the repository, so no transcription could be checked against anything; an external audit was right to reject the resulting decoder and validator theorems.

lean.note: elan-installed toolchain reports exactly this commit.

leanPackages.note: Proof core uses only Lean core and Std. No network-fetched proof inputs.
